item.description: Peptide-oligonucleotide conjugates can unite DNA nanotechnology with peptide self-assembly to create new and unusual nanostructures. We have created the first conjugate of DNA to a Waltz peptide – a class of β-sheet peptides which are important in the study of biological amyloids. Multi-micrometer rods have been identified which are attributable to peptide-dominated assembly. These results could lead to new ways to interface with amyloid, as well as demonstrating the range of self-assembled structures possible with DNA-peptide conjugates.

item.title: The inhibition mechanism of aldehyde dehydrogenase 1A3 by the antitumor drug DIMATE
item.description: Aldehyde dehydrogenase 1A (ALDH1A) enzymes play central roles in retinoic acid signaling and cancer stem cell biology, yet the molecular determinants governing isoform-selective covalent inhibition remain poorly understood. Here we investigate the binding and reactivity of the activated alkyne inhibitor S-methyl-4-(dimethylamino)-4-methylpent-2-ynethioate (DIMATE), a potent, irreversible inhibitor of ALDH1A currently in phase I clinical trials. Using QM/MM metadynamics simulations based on high-resolution crystal structures, enzyme kinetics and site-directed mutagenesis, we found that active-site cysteine reactivity and cofactor-binding channel occupancy control whether the inhibitor binds reversibly or irreversibly to the ALDH1A3 isoform. We identified two reaction pathways initiated by nucleophilic attack from the catalytic Cys314: transthioesterification at the carbonyl carbon and α-addition to the alkyne. Only the α-addition leads to irreversible inhibition, a process that critically depends on a vicinal cysteine (Cys313) acting as a proton donor. Consistently, experiments show that ALDH1A isoforms lacking this neighboring cysteine, as well as Cys313Ala mutants, display exclusively reversible inhibition. NAD+ binding further modulates reactivity by disfavoring α-addition and promoting hydrolysis of DIMATE to a non-inhibitory carboxylic acid product, establishing NAD+ as a switch between irreversible covalent modification and reversible turnover. Together, these results reveal how vicinal cysteine chemistry and cofactor-dependent activesite dynamics govern covalent reactivity in ALDH1A enzymes, providing a basis for the rational design of isoform-selective covalent inhibitors targeting cancer-associated ALDH enzymes.

item.title: Growth dynamics and pore trapping in lithium metal electrodes
item.description: Achieving high energy density in lithium metal cells requires minimizing both the electrolyte volume and the excess lithium metal. To ensure acceptable cycle life under these conditions, a dense electrode morphology is a necessity. External stack pressure is a common route to mitigate the development of a porous morphology, however, the electrode porosity still tends to increase during extended cycling. In this work, operando X-ray nano-tomography is used to track the pore evolution with sub-micron spatial resolution and visualize its dependence on stack pressure. A pore formation mechanism is unveiled, based on highly localized initial Li deposition on the uneven electrode surface that develops during cycling. Newly deposited structures grow rapidly and when in contact with the separator, the pressure transmitted induces horizontal growth, coarsening the structures. This type of growth mechanism traps pores between the bulk electrode and a dense layer of columnar lithium. Based on this, a homogeneous initial deposition in each cycle should be targeted to suppress pore trapping, thereby minimizing both the electrode surface area and the required electrolyte volume.

item.title: Spontaneous defect formation as the origin of superionic transitions in antifluorite-type structures
item.description: Solid-state electrolytes offer the possibility of safer and higher energy density batteries, yet only a limited number of materials achieve ionic conductivities suitable for practical applications. Type-II superionic conductors, which undergo continuous temperature-driven transitions between low and high ionic conductivity regimes are strong candidates for high-performance solid state electrolytes, but the transition mechanism is not sufficiently understood. In this study, we investigate the archetypical superionic conductors Li2O and Li2S with the antifluorite structure using long-time-scale molecular dynamics simulations with an Allegro machine-learning force field (MLFF) trained on density functional theory data selected using an on-the-fly active learning procedure. To this end, superionic transitions are identified around 1450 K for Li2O and around 1100 K for Li2S through continuous peaks in the heat capacity. Diffusion coefficients and concentration of Frenkel defects are found to exhibit strong non-Arrhenius behavior coinciding with the superionic transition where both diffusion activation energy and defect formation energy decrease significantly across the transition. This suggests a self-enhanced spontaneous defect formation mechanism, which drives the superionic transition and promotes increased ionic diffusion. These results identifies the microscopic origin of type-II superionic behavior as a result of correlated defect formation and support the design of improved solid-state electrolytes.

item.title: Cost-effective nanorough black nickel-based SERS substrates with statistically validated spatial uniformity
item.description: Reliable surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) substrates must combine high enhancement with spatially uniform and reproducible responses. Here, hierarchical rough black nickel (b-Ni) substrates were fabricated by electrodeposition and acid etching and coated with Ag or Au layers (5–50 nm). Their SERS performance was systematically evaluated using 4-mercaptobenzoic acid (4-MBA) and large-area Raman mapping (1.5 × 1.5 mm2; 900 spectra per substrate), supported by statistical analysis of signal intensity, spatial variability, response distribution, and inter-band correlation. Metrics included median signed band areas, relative standard deviation (RSD), the median absolute deviation (MAD)-based coefficient of variation, the contribution of the 10% highest-response positions to the total positive response, and Spearman’s rank correlation coefficient. Ag-coated b-Ni substrates exhibited substantially stronger and more spatially uniform enhancement than Au-coated substrates, with performance increasing with Ag thickness. The 50 nm b-Ni/Ag architecture provided the optimal combination of signal strength and spatial reproducibility. Control experiments with bare b-Ni and flat Ag and Au films deposited on polished silicon confirmed that the enhancement arises from the synergistic effect of hierarchical b-Ni micro/nanoroughness and the plasmonic noble-metal coating. These results establish Ag-coated b-Ni as a simple, low-cost, and scalable platform for robust SERS measurements, reducing the need for extensive spatial screening.

item.title: Binding Mode of the Heterocyclic Amine 2-Amino-9H-pyrido[2,3-b] indole (AαC) to DNA Elucidated by Molecular Docking and Molecular Dynamics Simulation
item.description: Background: 2-Amino-9H-pyrido[2,3-b]indole (AαC) is a mutagenic and carcinogenic heterocyclic aromatic amine formed by pyrolysis of proteins in cooked meat and present in tobacco smoke. After metabolic activation to a reactive nitrenium ion, it modifies DNA covalently, mainly at guanine. How AαC first associates with DNA, before any covalent bond forms, is not well understood. Methods: We docked AαC to three B-DNA dodecamers (PDB IDs 1BNA, 2Z2G and 2HKC) with PatchDock and FireDock, and ran explicit-solvent molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of the docked complexes in NAMD 2.13 with the CHARMM36 force field (1BNA: 10 ns; 2Z2G: 50 ns; NPT, 300 K, 0.15 M NaCl). Results: AαC bound in the minor groove of all three dodecamers, with global binding energies of -50.08 (1BNA), -53.41 (2Z2G) and -45.22 kcal/mol (2HKC). Atomic van der Waals terms contributed -16.41 to -18.36 kcal/mol, and single hydrogen bonds to thymine, guanine or adenine oxygen atoms were identified (2.2–2.8 Å). In the simulations AαC remained bound with a low, stable backbone RMSD, whereas the DNA backbone fluctuated considerably more. The minor-groove poses were poorly oriented for covalent attack when the base pairs were intact and canonical. Conclusions: Neutral AαC forms stable, groove-bound non-covalent complexes with B-DNA, but these complexes do not by themselves position the amine for C8-guanine adduct formation. Local distortion of the DNA, or the charged nitrenium ion, may be required. The complexes presented here serve as starting structures for ongoing quantum-mechanical studies of nitrenium ion stability and covalent adduct formation.
